title: Print a shared node once
starter:
type e = Lit of int | Var of string | Add of e * e | Mul of e * e

let emit (e : e) : string list * string =
  let lines = ref [] in
  let names : (e * string) list ref = ref [] in
  let rec go e =
    match e with
    | Lit n -> string_of_int n
    | Var s -> s
    | Add (a, b) | Mul (a, b) ->
      let x = go a in
      let y = go b in
      let op = match e with Add _ -> "+" | _ -> "*" in
      let v = Printf.sprintf "v%d" (List.length !lines) in
      lines := Printf.sprintf "int32_t %s = (int32_t)((uint32_t)%s %s (uint32_t)%s);" v x op y :: !lines;
      v
  in
  let result = go e in
  ignore names;
  (List.rev !lines, result)

tests.expr: (let x = Add (Var "a", Lit 1) in emit (Mul (x, x)))
(let rec dbl n e = if n = 0 then e else (let d = dbl (n - 1) e in Add (d, d)) in emit (dbl 3 (Var "x")))
tests.expect: int32_t v0 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)x + (uint32_t)x); | int32_t v1 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 + (uint32_t)v0); | int32_t v2 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v1 + (uint32_t)v1); => v2

tests.expr: (let s = Add (Var "a", Lit 1) in emit (Add (Mul (s, Lit 2), Mul (s, Lit 3))))
tests.expect: int32_t v0 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)1); | int32_t v1 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 * (uint32_t)2); | int32_t v2 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 * (uint32_t)3); | int32_t v3 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v1 + (uint32_t)v2); => v3

tests.expr: (let v () = Var (String.make 1 'a') in emit (Mul (Add (v (), Lit 1), Add (v (), Lit 1))))
tests.expect: int32_t v0 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)1); | int32_t v1 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)a + (uint32_t)1); | int32_t v2 = (int32_t)((uint32_t)v0 * (uint32_t)v1); => v2

tests.expr: (let rec dbl n e = if n = 0 then e else (let d = dbl (n - 1) e in Add (d, d)) in let (ls, r) = emit (dbl 12 (Var "x")) in ([string_of_int (List.length ls)], r))

hints: The table `names` is there and nothing uses it yet. It should pair a node you have already printed with the C name you gave it.
`List.assq_opt e !names` looks a node up with `==`, which asks whether two values are the very same node. Two nodes that were built separately stay separate even when they look equal.
Wrap the branch: `match List.assq_opt e !names with Some v -> v | None -> ...` and, in the `None` case, add `names := (e, v) :: !names;` just before the final `v`.
explain: The reference looks the node up in `names` with `List.assq_opt` before it walks into the sources, and returns the saved name when it is there. After printing a line it saves the pair of node and name. A node used twice is now printed once, and because the lookup comes first, its sources are not walked a second time either.
